Ardglas railway station (site), County DownOpened in 1892 as the terminus of the Belfast & County Down Railway's line from Downpatrick, this station closed in 1950.
View west from near the former buffers.

images.caption: Old railway station,  Ardglass. The nine-mile branch from Downpatrick to Ardglass opened in 1892 and closed in 1950  a very short existence.  The photo shows Ardglass station 56 years after closure  passenger station on the left, goods shed on the right.  The line continued (behind the photographer) to the harbour.  That section closed some time in the 1920s.

images.caption: ArdglassArdglass opened in 1892 as the terminus of the Downpatrick, Killough & Ardglass Railway. It closed, along with the line in 1950 as part of the UTA's savage closure programme, leaving the County Down fishing village without a railway.
